sources.title: What is Redis? In-memory database, cache, and message broker
What is Redis? In-Memory Database, Features, Data Structures, and Use Cases | Lenovo US
In-memory cache explained simply for fast apps

results.insert:
Redis is an open-source, in-memory data structure store that can serve not only as a cache but also as a database, message broker, and streaming engine. It belongs to the NoSQL family of key/value stores, where unique keys map to values of various data types. ([redis.io](https://redis.io/tutorials/what-is-redis))

It is widely adopted for its sub-millisecond response times and rich data structures, including strings, hashes, lists, and sets, making it well suited for real-time applications. ([redis.io](https://redis.io/tutorials/what-is-redis), [lenovo.com](https://www.lenovo.com/us/en/glossary/redis))

Unlike Memcached, which is purely in-memory and loses all data on restart, Redis offers optional persistence, allowing it to recover state after a reboot or be backed up for durability. ([redis.io](https://redis.io/glossary/in-memory-cache))
